title: an object-literal shorthand method and an object-literal getter may each abort with panic(...)
notes: specification/failures.mdx §Panic Does Not Widen a Return Type: 'Calling `panic(...)` MUST NOT force a function's return type to widen into `Result<A, Panic>`.' and 'A function that validates an argument, refuses a forgery, or asserts an invariant MUST therefore be able to abort with `panic(...)` while keeping a plain return type.' docs/DECISIONS.md carries the matching Locked entry ('Calling `panic(...)` does not widen a return type into `Result<A, Panic>` … the prohibition is on the compiler forcing it'). `E` is the expected-error channel (reference/function-channels.mdx) and a panic is not an expected error, so a construct that aborts with `panic(...)` keeps whatever return type it declares. Object literals are a separate walk from class members in both implementations and were separately broken (SMITHERS1101 plus SMITHERS1303 on the method, SMITHERS1101 plus SMITHERS1105 on the getter for the reference). The getter's body here is a bare `panic(...)` with no other statement, which is also the smallest function whose entire body is an abort — the form a lowering that guesses a return value gets wrong.
